item.text: I’m narrowing this to federal actions and crisis response that actually touch physical safety: policing accountability, hate-crime and mass-violence response, protest posture, and whether Biden personally incited or tolerated domestic fear. I’ll keep the local repression priors in view but won’t re-litigate them as if they were new evidence.

item.text:
Severity class: recurring domestic violence, hate-motivated violence, political intimidation, and localized abuse. I do not see evidence of systematic state terror in 2022. Attribution is mixed: Biden directly set some federal rules and messaging, while much of the underlying harm remained state/local or societal rather than federally directed.

**Reused evidence**
None.

**New evidence**
- Biden’s Jan. 6 anniversary remarks are the clearest direct anti-incitement baseline: he condemned political violence, said the Capitol attack tried to block a peaceful transfer of power, and rejected normalization of violence as a political tool.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Remarks on the First Anniversary of the Insurrection at the United States Capitol","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-01-06","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-the-first-anniversary-the-insurrection-the-united-states-capitol","claim":"Biden said democracy had been attacked on January 6, that a violent mob tried to prevent the peaceful transfer of power, and that such an attack must never happen again.","locator":"lines 63-65","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary presidential transcript with exact date and direct statements.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and about domestic political violence.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden statement.","contrary_evidence":["The speech is retrospective and rhetorical rather than an operational policy order.","It shows condemnation of violence, not a full remedy record."],"lenses":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10"]}

- The Philadelphia democracy speech is a stronger late-year anti-violence and anti-intimidation statement, explicitly rejecting political violence, warning against election intimidation, and distinguishing dissent from violence.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Address on United States Democracy in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-09-01","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/address-united-states-democracy-philadelphia-pennsylvania","claim":"Biden said political violence has no place in America, that election officials and poll workers had faced intimidation and death threats, and that politics should remain disagreement, debate, and dissent rather than violence.","locator":"lines 103-111","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary presidential transcript with explicit anti-violence language and direct political framing.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden statement.","contrary_evidence":["The speech uses very sharp partisan language, which can intensify polarization.","It is still rhetoric; it does not by itself prove effective protection on the ground."],"lenses":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10"]}

- Executive Order 14074 is the best federal-policing reform source in the batch. It requires fair treatment, accountability, use-of-force data, early-warning systems, anti-bias training, no-knock limits, and misconduct records.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Executive Order 14074—Advancing Effective, Accountable Policing and Criminal Justice Practices To Enhance Public Trust and Public Safety","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-05-25","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-14074-advancing-effective-accountable-policing-and-criminal-justice","claim":"The order required federal law enforcement agencies to emphasize fair and impartial justice, collect and publish use-of-force data, adopt early-warning systems, restrict no-knock entries, ban chokeholds and carotid restraints in federal agencies, and create stronger misconduct-accountability procedures.","locator":"lines 64-65 and 151-180","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary executive order text with detailed operational requirements.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and targeted at federal law-enforcement conduct.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden executive order.","contrary_evidence":["It governs federal agencies, not all state and local police.","Implementation quality is not the same as the order’s text."],"lenses":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6"]}

- Uvalde is the clearest domestic-crisis response. Biden described mass shootings as a uniquely American carnage, called for action, and pushed Congress to act on gun laws.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Remarks on the Shooting in Uvalde, Texas","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-05-24","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-the-shooting-uvalde-texas","claim":"Biden said mass shootings occur in America with unmatched frequency, urged the country to act, and framed commonsense gun laws as necessary to reduce carnage.","locator":"lines 77-85","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary presidential transcript at the moment of a major domestic crisis.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden response to a domestic mass-casualty event.","contrary_evidence":["This is crisis rhetoric, not a completed policy effect.","It addresses gun violence broadly rather than a specific enforcement failure."],"lenses":["3B.6","3B.9","3B.10"]}

- The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act is the year’s major gun-safety law and the clearest concrete protection action after Uvalde and Buffalo.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Remarks on Signing the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and an Exchange With Reporters","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-06-25","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-signing-the-bipartisan-safer-communities-act-and-exchange-with-reporters","claim":"Biden signed the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and said the law would save lives, calling it a major response to gun violence.","locator":"lines 71-72 and 82-88","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary bill-signing transcript with direct policy action and stated intent.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden signature and policy choice.","contrary_evidence":["The law is narrower than broader gun-control advocates wanted.","Legislative passage does not guarantee measurable short-term harm reduction."],"lenses":["3B.6","3B.9","3B.10"]}

- Independent media corroboration on the gun bill is useful because it frames the law as the first major federal gun reform in three decades.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Biden signs bipartisan gun safety package into law","publisher":"ABC News","publication_date":"2022-06-25","url":"https://abcnews.go.com/US/biden-signs-bipartisan-gun-safety-package-law/story?id=85692952","claim":"AP reporting said Biden signed the first major federal gun reform in three decades after the Uvalde shooting.","locator":"opening paragraph and lead","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous AP reporting carried by ABC News; independent of the White House record.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Directly about Biden’s signing and policy choice.","contrary_evidence":["The article is a news summary, not the statute itself.","The law is significant but limited relative to wider gun-control demands."],"lenses":["3B.6","3B.9","3B.10"]}

- The Emmett Till Antilynching Act is the clearest 2022 anti-hate-violence measure, making lynching a federal hate crime for the first time.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Remarks on Signing the Emmett Till Antilynching Act","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-03-29","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-signing-the-emmett-till-antilynching-act","claim":"Biden signed the Emmett Till Antilynching Act and said it made lynching a federal hate crime for the first time in American history.","locator":"lines 74 and 83-84","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary signing transcript with direct legal action and explicit statement.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden signature and policy choice.","contrary_evidence":["This addresses hate-crime law, not all forms of domestic violence.","Law passage does not prove enforcement effectiveness."],"lenses":["3B.1","3B.3","3B.7","3B.10"]}

- VAWA reauthorization shows Biden’s long-run emphasis on changing the culture around domestic abuse and supporting survivors with police and training infrastructure.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Remarks on Reauthorization of the Violence Against Women Act","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-03-16","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-reauthorization-the-violence-against-women-act","claim":"Biden said the goal was to change the culture around violence against women, provide more protection against domestic violence, stalking, and sexual assault, and support survivors in finding ways out of abuse.","locator":"lines 66-69 and 83-93","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary remarks directly about domestic-violence prevention and survivor protection.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden statement and long-standing policy priority.","contrary_evidence":["The remarks are partly retrospective and personal in tone.","They do not show full 2022 implementation outcomes."],"lenses":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.10"]}

- The Domestic Violence Awareness Month proclamation adds a contemporaneous 2022 executive statement about ensuring survivors have justice and support.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Proclamation 10461—National Domestic Violence Awareness and Prevention Month, 2022","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-09-30","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-10461-national-domestic-violence-awareness-and-prevention-month-2022","claim":"Biden proclaimed October 2022 Domestic Violence Awareness Month and said the administration was working to ensure survivors had access to justice and support for healing and well-being.","locator":"lines 66-66","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary presidential proclamation with direct policy framing.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden proclamation.","contrary_evidence":["A proclamation is symbolic unless tied to concrete enforcement or services.","It does not by itself measure domestic-violence prevalence."],"lenses":["3B.7","3B.10"]}

- The United We Stand summit is Biden’s strongest 2022 whole-of-society anti-hate response.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"FACT SHEET: The United We Stand Summit: Taking Action to Prevent and Address Hate-Motivated Violence and Foster Unity","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-09-15","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/fact-sheet-the-united-we-stand-summit-taking-action-prevent-and-address-hate-motivated","claim":"The White House said Biden was hosting the summit to counter hate-fueled violence, honor communities hit by attacks and mass shootings, and announce new cross-sector actions to prevent and respond to hate-driven violence.","locator":"lines 62-75","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary White House fact sheet with specific commitments and coalition-building measures.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden-hosted initiative.","contrary_evidence":["A summit is a signaling and coordination step, not a guaranteed safety outcome.","It focuses on hate-fueled violence rather than all domestic violence."],"lenses":["3B.3","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9"]}

- DOJ’s election-threat work shows the administration treated threats against election workers as a real domestic-safety problem.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Readout of Election Threats Task Force Briefing with Election Officials and Workers","publisher":"United States Department of Justice","publication_date":"2022-08-01","url":"https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/readout-election-threats-task-force-briefing-election-officials-and-workers","claim":"The Election Threats Task Force had reviewed over 1,000 hostile or harassing contacts reported by the election community, and only about 11% met the threshold for a federal criminal investigation.","locator":"lines 139-143","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous DOJ operational update with concrete figures.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect but strong; this is DOJ action under Biden’s administration.","contrary_evidence":["The figures show the scale of threats, not Biden’s personal authorship of them.","Many contacts were hostile but not criminal threats."],"lenses":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9"]}

- DOJ’s national hate-crime initiative gives another concrete federal response to domestic intimidation and bias violence.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Justice Department Launches Nationwide Initiative to Combat Unlawful Acts of Hate","publisher":"United States Department of Justice","publication_date":"2022-09-15","url":"https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-launches-nationwide-initiative-combat-unlawful-acts-hate","claim":"All 94 U.S. Attorneys’ Offices were to host outreach and community engagement programs to address and prevent unlawful acts of hate over the next year.","locator":"lines 139-147","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous DOJ press release with nationwide scope and implementation plan.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect but strong; this is a federal response under Biden’s administration.","contrary_evidence":["It is an initiative, not proof of reduction in hate crimes.","It does not address every source of domestic violence or intimidation."],"lenses":["3B.1","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9"]}

- The Respect for Marriage Act matters here because it gives vulnerable couples a clearer legal and social safety baseline in the face of post-Dobbs uncertainty.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Press Release: Bills Signed: H.R. 8404","publisher":"The American Presidency Project","publication_date":"2022-12-13","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/press-release-bills-signed-hr-8404","claim":"Biden signed the Respect for Marriage Act, which establishes statutory authority for same-sex and interracial marriages and repeals contrary federal barriers.","locator":"lines 63-65","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary bill-signing press release with direct legal effect.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Biden signature and policy choice.","contrary_evidence":["This is civil-rights protection more than a classic physical-safety measure.","It protects status and family security rather than policing violence directly."],"lenses":["3B.7","3B.10"]}

- The FBI hate-crime statistics page is useful contrary context: 2022 hate crimes rose, showing Biden inherited a still-dangerous environment that policy could not fully reverse in-year.  
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"2022 FBI Hate Crimes Statistics","publisher":"U.S. Department of Justice","publication_date":"2023-10-30","url":"https://www.justice.gov/archives/crs/highlights/2022-hate-crime-statistics","claim":"The DOJ summarized FBI data showing hate-crime incidents increased by 794 in 2022 to 11,634, with race-based, religion-based, and anti-LGBTQ incidents remaining substantial.","locator":"lines 128-135","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official DOJ summary of FBI reporting, with specific 2022 figures.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Retrospective publication about 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Country-level context, not direct Biden conduct.","contrary_evidence":["Published after 2022, so it is retrospective context rather than contemporaneous evidence.","It reflects reporting by law enforcement agencies, so undercounting remains possible."],"lenses":["3B.1","3B.7","3B.10"]}

**Search and rejection summary**
I screened roughly 30 documents across the White House / APP, DOJ, GovInfo, FBI/DOJ archives, and a small number of independent media reports. I kept sources that directly touched physical safety, intimidation, hate violence, policing accountability, gun violence, survivor protection, or vulnerable-group protection.

I rejected or deprioritized:
- Repeated versions of the same presidential speech when they added no new factual claim.
- Out-of-period items from 2021 or 2023+ unless they were used only as retrospective context.
- General domestic-policy material that did not connect to violence, abuse, intimidation, or protection.
- Purely symbolic remarks where there was no clear safety nexus.
- Broad political commentary that lacked a concrete domestic-safety claim.
- Overlapping election-threat and hate-crime pages when one stronger DOJ source already covered the same point.

**Remaining gaps**
- I do not have a direct 2022 source on federal prison or detention conditions that would materially change 3B attribution.
- I do not have a strong 2022 record showing whether Biden’s federal policing reforms were implemented effectively inside agencies, only that he issued them.
- Protest treatment is mostly evidenced by rhetoric and election-protection work, not by a large set of enforcement records.
- The biggest missing piece is a clearer before/after empirical link between Biden’s actions and year-end domestic safety outcomes.
- If you want a fuller 3B dossier, the next useful search would be on FBI domestic-terrorism cases, DOJ civil-rights enforcement outcomes, and any 2022 federal responses to abortion-clinic violence or anti-LGBTQ threats.
